header.title: De anima libri mantissa: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Alexander of Aphrodisias
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg0732.tlg011.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0732.tlg011.1st1K-gr: ‘The very people who are also the cause of their art’ is taken to mean the credulous many, whose weakness (described just before) makes the pretended art possible; the referent is not certain.

nodes.text: And taking as their helpers the very people who are also the cause of their art, they persuade most men, setting upon them in their difficulties and misfortunes, when they all but pray that this should prove to be so; and through a certain practice and understanding of such matters, and study of the sequence of events in such cases, they shrewdly foretell some of the things that will follow in consequence for people in that situation, claiming of course that they have this from the art concerned with fate, and collecting no small fees for such malpractice, while those who consult them gladly pay them as helpers and advocates of their own faults.
